title: Line Atlas: graduate-level astrophysical spectral-line catalogue

conventions.wavelength_medium: Vacuum throughout. Familiar air wavelengths are mentioned only in observational notes.
conventions.rest_value_policy: Radio/submillimetre entries use laboratory rest frequency; infrared/UV/optical entries use vacuum wavelength; X-ray and gamma-ray entries may use photon energy when that is the operational convention.
conventions.canonical_wavelength_angstrom: A convenience conversion. Null for cm/mm rotational or hyperfine lines, where frequency is the unambiguous observing quantity.
conventions.temperature_policy: Ranges describe common emitting/absorbing gas or approximate CIE abundance peaks, not a unique formation temperature. Photoionized gas can produce the same ion at very different kinetic temperature.
conventions.density_policy: Critical/effective densities are order-of-magnitude guidance and depend on collider, temperature, optical depth, radiation field, and molecular column.
conventions.ionization_energy_policy: For ions, lower_stage_to_species is the threshold to create the listed ion from the next-lower charge state; species_to_next_stage is the threshold to ionize it further. Values are in eV and rounded from NIST ASD where supplied.

entries.temperature_regime: CNM roughly 20-200 K; WNM roughly 5000-10000 K; detectable outside strict LTE
entries.density_sensitivity: Not a conventional density diagnostic. Emission gives optically thin H I column; emission plus absorption constrains spin temperature and covering fraction.
entries.observational_notes: Rest frequency is exceptionally precise. State the radio/optical/relativistic velocity convention and reference frame. Self-absorption and optical depth can hide cold gas.

entries.mechanism: lambda-doubling plus hyperfine transition; often masing
tracers: molecular gas magnetic field via Zeeman splitting
entries.temperature_regime: typically tens to hundreds of kelvin; non-LTE pumping controls masers
entries.density_sensitivity: Population inversion depends on FIR pump, OH column and density; not a simple one-number density tracer.
entries.observational_notes: Compare 1665:1667 and satellite-line ratios to diagnose LTE departures, pumping and opacity. Strongly affected by radio-frequency interference in some bands.

entries.mechanism: lambda-doubling plus hyperfine transition; thermal absorption/emission or maser
entries.temperature_regime: typically 10-300 K, with excitation set by collisions and radiative pumping
entries.density_sensitivity: Line ratios are excitation/opacity diagnostics rather than direct density meters.
entries.observational_notes: The 1667-MHz line usually dominates extragalactic OH megamasers. Hyperfine LTE expectations can fail spectacularly under FIR pumping.

entries.temperature_regime: commonly about 300-1000 K for strong collisional pumping
entries.density_sensitivity: Maser inversion favors very dense gas, often n(H2) about 10^7-10^10 cm^-3, but geometry and velocity coherence dominate brightness.
entries.observational_notes: Brightness temperature is non-thermal and cannot be interpreted as kinetic temperature. Narrow spikes vary and may be highly beamed.

entries.temperature_regime: especially effective near 8-40 K, but present in warmer dense gas
entries.density_sensitivity: Effective excitation densities are typically around 10^3 cm^-3 and model dependent; hyperfine anomalies can affect opacity estimates.
entries.observational_notes: Fit the full hyperfine structure. The (2,2)/(1,1) rotational temperature is converted to kinetic temperature with a collisional model.

entries.temperature_regime: roughly 15-100 K for common applications; higher metastable lines extend the thermometer
entries.density_sensitivity: Similar effective-density scale to (1,1), with excitation dependent on temperature and NH3 column.
entries.observational_notes: Use matched beams and simultaneous calibration when deriving temperatures; (2,2) may miss the coldest component at low signal-to-noise.

environments: inner envelopes of oxygen-rich AGB stars
entries.temperature_regime: warm to hot molecular gas, often about 1000-2000 K near evolved stars
entries.density_sensitivity: Requires high density and an inversion; representative pumping solutions use n(H2) around 10^9-10^10 cm^-3.
entries.observational_notes: Non-LTE, polarized and time variable. Do not use maser flux as a linear mass estimator.

entries.temperature_regime: commonly 10-100 K; IR pumping can matter in luminous dusty nuclei
entries.density_sensitivity: Optically thin critical density is of order 10^6 cm^-3 near 10-20 K, while trapping makes effective excitation densities commonly 1-2 dex lower.
entries.observational_notes: Resolve or model three hyperfine components in narrow Galactic sources. Opacity, abundance, electron excitation and 14-micron pumping complicate the dense-gas interpretation.

entries.mechanism: electric-dipole rotational transition of a molecular ion
entries.temperature_regime: about 10-100 K in most applications
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is a few 10^5 cm^-3, but effective excitation density can be around 10^3-10^4 cm^-3 depending on opacity and column.
entries.observational_notes: Often optically thick and self-absorbed. Pair with H13CO+ to estimate opacity; abundance is sensitive to ionization and water/CO chemistry.

entries.mechanism: electric-dipole rotational transition with nitrogen hyperfine structure
entries.temperature_regime: especially useful around 7-30 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is roughly 10^5 cm^-3; radiative trapping and hyperfine excitation lower the effective threshold.
entries.observational_notes: The quoted value is a conventional reference for the hyperfine complex; precision velocity work must adopt component-specific frequencies and a consistent catalog.

entries.temperature_regime: about 10-100 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is a few 10^5 cm^-3, with a substantially lower effective excitation density for optically thick bright columns.
entries.observational_notes: CS can deplete in cold cores and become optically thick; use isotopologues and multi-J excitation rather than a single conversion factor.

entries.temperature_regime: cold molecular gas, commonly 8-50 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is around 10^3 cm^-3 and effective excitation density lower; abundance and shielding often dominate detectability.
entries.observational_notes: Usually thinner than 13CO but not guaranteed optically thin. Selective photodissociation, fractionation and isotope-ratio gradients bias mass estimates.

entries.temperature_regime: commonly 8-100 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is around 10^3 cm^-3; photon trapping lowers the effective excitation threshold.
entries.observational_notes: Often optically thick in cloud peaks. Carbon isotope gradients, chemical fractionation and selective photodissociation prevent a universal 12CO/13CO abundance ratio.

tracers: bulk molecular gas via CO-to-H2 conversion
entries.temperature_regime: cold molecular gas from about 5 K upward; upper-state energy is 5.53 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Optically thin critical density is roughly 2x10^3 cm^-3, while trapping permits bright emission at a few 10^2 cm^-3 or below.
entries.observational_notes: Usually optically thick. X_CO depends on metallicity, dynamics, excitation, spatial scale and radiation field; CMB contrast matters at high redshift.

entries.temperature_regime: cold to moderately warm gas; upper-state energy is 16.6 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is around 10^4 cm^-3, but opacity makes the effective density much lower.
entries.observational_notes: Brightness-temperature ratio r21 is sensitive to excitation, beam filling and optical depth. Match angular resolution before interpreting line ratios.

entries.temperature_regime: commonly 20-100 K; upper-state energy is 33.2 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is a few 10^4 cm^-3; radiative trapping lowers the effective density.
entries.observational_notes: Mid-J selection can bias samples toward excited gas. Use a CO SLED and consistent beam/uv coverage to infer multiple gas phases.

entries.temperature_regime: cold molecular gas, commonly 15-60 K; upper level is 23.6 K above ground
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density with H2 is of order 5x10^2 cm^-3, weakly model dependent.
entries.observational_notes: The two [C I] lines give an excitation temperature only under a common, often optically thin one-zone assumption. Carbon abundance is not universal.

entries.temperature_regime: typically 25-100 K; upper level is 62.5 K above ground
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density with H2 is of order 10^3 cm^-3.
entries.observational_notes: The line sits close to CO(7-6) in frequency, useful for simultaneous setups but demanding correct identification at uncertain redshift.

entries.temperature_regime: upper level corresponds to 91.2 K; excited in neutral and ionized gas from roughly 50 K to 10^4 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Approximate critical densities: about 50 cm^-3 for electrons, 3x10^3 for H and 5x10^3 for H2, with temperature dependence.
paired_or_diagnostic_lines: [N II] 205 micron to isolate ionized contribution
entries.observational_notes: A multiphase line, not a pure PDR or SFR tracer. Optical depth, foreground absorption and the high-surface-brightness [C II] deficit affect interpretation.

entries.temperature_regime: ionized gas near 6000-10000 K; excitation energy is only about 70 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is roughly 40-50 cm^-3; the 122/205 ratio measures electron density over roughly 1-10^3 cm^-3.
entries.observational_notes: N+ requires ionized gas because its formation threshold exceeds 13.6 eV. Low critical density makes 205 micron particularly sensitive to diffuse ionized material.

entries.temperature_regime: ionized gas around 6000-10000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is about 300 cm^-3; 122/205 is a robust density ratio when both lines sample the same gas.
entries.observational_notes: Far-IR dust extinction is small, but aperture mismatch and multi-density structure can bias the ratio.

environments: neutral gas near H II regions
tracers: PDR density and radiation field with [O I] 63/[C II]
entries.temperature_regime: warm neutral gas, commonly about 100-1000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density for H/H2 collisions is of order 10^5 cm^-3, model dependent.
entries.observational_notes: Usually weaker but less self-absorbed than the 63-micron line. The 63/145 ratio can reveal opacity, foreground absorption, temperature and density.

tracers: dominant neutral-gas cooling in warm dense regions
entries.temperature_regime: upper level is about 228 K; strongest in gas roughly 100-1000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density for collisions with H is roughly 5x10^5 cm^-3; optical depth often matters first.
entries.observational_notes: Can be optically thick and self-absorbed by colder foreground O I; a line deficit does not uniquely imply weak PDR heating.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 7000-20000 K; low excitation energy minimizes temperature sensitivity
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is about 500 cm^-3; 52/88 measures densities from roughly 10^2 to 10^4 cm^-3.
entries.observational_notes: Bright in hard, low-metallicity H II regions and relatively extinction-free. Abundance, ionization parameter and density all affect line-to-SFR conversions.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 7000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is roughly 3.6x10^3 cm^-3; 52/88 is a standard far-IR density diagnostic.
entries.observational_notes: Use matched apertures. At high density both lines approach LTE and the ratio saturates; abundance and ionization structure remain separate uncertainties.

entries.temperature_regime: warm neutral or ionized gas, about 100-10000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is roughly 10^3 cm^-3 for electrons and a few 10^5 cm^-3 for H, with temperature dependence.
entries.observational_notes: Silicon depletion and grain destruction dominate absolute calibration; strong emission may arise from multiple phases along the same sightline.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 5000-15000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is of order 10^3 cm^-3; the 18.7/33.5 ratio spans roughly 10^2-10^4 cm^-3.
entries.observational_notes: The widely separated pair is susceptible to aperture and extinction mismatch; use the correct low-density limit for the adopted atomic data.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 5000-15000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is roughly 2x10^4 cm^-3; 18.7/33.5 rises with density before saturating.
entries.observational_notes: Less affected by dust than optical lines but can suffer silicate-feature continuum systematics and aperture differences.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 5000-15000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is of order 6x10^5 cm^-3; usually in the low-density limit for extended H II gas.
entries.observational_notes: [Ne III]/[Ne II] is sensitive to ionizing hardness and ionization parameter, but also geometry, metallicity and stellar population age.

tracers: ionization parameter with other neon lines
entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 7000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is about 10^5 cm^-3; typically low-density in integrated galaxies.
entries.observational_notes: Neon is only weakly depleted, but the ratio to [Ne II] is not a one-parameter hardness indicator.

entries.temperature_regime: sensitive to roughly 80-300 K gas; upper-state energy is about 510 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density depends on H, H2 and He collision rates, typically around 10^2-10^3 cm^-3 at warm temperatures.
entries.observational_notes: Quadrupole emission is optically thin but weak. Warm-H2 mass is exponentially sensitive to assumed temperature and ortho-to-para ratio.

entries.temperature_regime: commonly traces about 150-700 K gas; upper-state energy is about 1015 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is typically around 10^3-10^4 cm^-3, depending strongly on collider and temperature.
entries.observational_notes: Multiple-temperature excitation diagrams are usually required; a single Boltzmann slope can hide non-LTE or mixed gas.

tracers: fluorescent versus thermal excitation with line ratios
entries.temperature_regime: roughly 1000-3000 K for thermal emission; UV fluorescence can populate it in cooler gas
entries.density_sensitivity: Thermalization requires densities roughly 10^4-10^6 cm^-3 depending on collider and temperature; ratios carry the diagnostic power.
entries.observational_notes: 2-1 S(1)/1-0 S(1) helps distinguish fluorescence from thermal shocks, but mixed excitation and differential extinction matter.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas near 5000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Case-B emissivity has modest density dependence over ordinary nebular conditions; high densities and optical depth alter decrements.
entries.observational_notes: Much less extinguished than H-alpha but fainter. Correct for underlying stellar absorption, extinction and broad/narrow component mixing.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas near 5000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Weak density dependence in Case B; departures arise at high density, high optical depth or strong collisional excitation.
entries.observational_notes: Ground-based access is difficult because of telluric absorption; space observations are powerful for heavily obscured star formation.

tracers: electron density with other [Fe II] lines
entries.temperature_regime: typically several thousand to about 15000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is of order 10^4-10^5 cm^-3; ratios among lines from different upper levels constrain density.
entries.observational_notes: The 1.257/1.644 ratio shares an upper level and is useful for extinction, but published A-values introduce systematic uncertainty.

rest_value.qualifier: strongest blended triplet component; air name 10830

entries.mechanism: permitted transition from the metastable triplet state
entries.temperature_regime: photoionized/recombining gas from roughly 5000 K upward; metastable population is radiation and density dependent
entries.density_sensitivity: Metastable 2s 3S population responds to electron density, ionization and radiative transfer; not a simple critical-density line.
entries.observational_notes: A multiplet with close components. Absorption can be saturated with partial covering; telluric correction and air/vacuum convention are essential.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 5000-15000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is high enough that normal H II regions are usually in the low-density regime; IR fine-structure lines provide stronger density leverage.
entries.observational_notes: Intrinsic 9533/9071 branching ratio is near 2.44 and can check calibration. Strong telluric absorption/fringing often dominates uncertainty.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 5000-15000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Usually below its critical density in ordinary nebulae; ratio to 9533 is fixed mainly by A-values.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value shown; the familiar air wavelength is about 9068.6 A. Correct for telluric absorption and use the theoretical branching ratio.

entries.mechanism: hydrogen recombination with possible collisional contribution
entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas near 5000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Case-B emissivity scales approximately with n_e n_p but the H-alpha/H-beta decrement is mainly extinction/transfer sensitive over ordinary nebular densities.
paired_or_diagnostic_lines: [N II] 6585 A and [S II] 6718/6733 A for BPT/shock diagnostics
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value shown; the traditional air wavelength is 6562.8 A. Dust, [N II] blending, stellar absorption, leakage and stochastic IMF sampling affect SFR estimates.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized or shocked gas around 6000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is roughly 10^5 cm^-3; usually in the low-density regime for normal H II regions.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 6583.45 A. N/O variations and ionization parameter limit one-dimensional metallicity calibrations.

entries.temperature_regime: roughly 5000-20000 K ionized or partially ionized gas
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density near 10^4 K is about 1.5x10^3 cm^-3; the doublet ratio is most useful around 10^2-10^4 cm^-3.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 6716.44 A. Ratio saturates at low and high density and can mix unresolved density phases.

entries.temperature_regime: roughly 5000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density near 10^4 K is about 4x10^3 cm^-3; paired ratio carries the density information.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 6730.82 A. Deblend both lines from sky residuals and broad H-alpha wings in complex nuclei.

entries.temperature_regime: warm neutral or partially ionized gas around several thousand to 20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Electron critical density is of order 2x10^6 cm^-3; collisional quenching matters in dense gas.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 6300.30 A. Bright terrestrial airglow demands careful sky subtraction, especially at low redshift.

entries.mechanism: helium recombination transition with collisional and radiative-transfer corrections
tracers: nebular physical conditions with other He I lines
entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 5000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: He I line ratios respond to electron density, optical depth in triplet lines and underlying absorption; multi-line fitting is required.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is about 5875.62 A. Correct for stellar absorption, Na sky features and triplet optical-depth effects.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas about 7000-20000 K; shocks can extend higher
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is about 7x10^5 cm^-3; the nebular-to-auroral ratio with 4364 A is strongly temperature sensitive.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 5006.84 A. Use the theoretical 5008/4960 ratio near 2.98 to test fits and saturation.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas about 7000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Same upper level and critical-density behavior as 5008 A.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 4958.91 A. Tie centroid, width and theoretical flux ratio to 5008 in multi-component fits when justified.

entries.mechanism: hydrogen recombination with possible collisional contribution
tracers: normalization for excitation and abundance ratios
entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas near 5000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Case-B ratios depend weakly on density over normal nebular conditions but change with temperature, optical depth and collisions.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 4861.33 A. Stellar Balmer absorption can severely bias weak emission and extinction estimates.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas commonly 10000-30000 K; shock zones can be hotter
entries.density_sensitivity: Recombination emissivity rather than a critical-density diagnostic; line width separates nebular and stellar components.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 4685.7 A. Broad stellar and narrow nebular He II require decomposition before inferring ionizing hardness.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas roughly 7000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is roughly 1.4x10^4 cm^-3 near 10^4 K; doublet ratio spans common nebular densities.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; traditional air wavelength is 3726.03 A. Unresolved surveys often quote [O II] 3727 for the sum—record that convention explicitly.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas roughly 7000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is roughly 3x10^3 cm^-3 near 10^4 K; ratio to 3727 saturates outside its useful density range.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; traditional air wavelength is 3728.82 A. Instrumental resolution and stellar continuum modeling determine whether the doublet yields useful densities.

tracers: ionization parameter with [O II] or [Ne II]
entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 8000-20000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Critical density is high, of order 10^7 cm^-3; generally in the low-density regime for H II regions.
entries.observational_notes: Vacuum value; familiar air wavelength is 3868.76 A. The weaker 3968-A partner blends with H-epsilon/Ca H in many spectra.

entries.temperature_regime: commonly about 10^4 K photoionized gas; not a unique thermometer
entries.density_sensitivity: Resonance absorption is column/ionization sensitive, not a critical-density diagnostic; emission is shaped by resonant scattering.
entries.observational_notes: Stronger doublet member with oscillator-strength ratio near 2. Saturation and partial covering drive the observed doublet ratio toward unity.

entries.temperature_regime: commonly about 10^4 K photoionized gas
entries.density_sensitivity: Not a direct density diagnostic; its value comes from doublet curve-of-growth and covering analysis.
entries.observational_notes: Weaker doublet member is essential for diagnosing saturation. Resonant emission infill can bias absorption equivalent widths.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 10000-30000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: The 1907/1909 ratio is density sensitive from low nebular densities into roughly 10^5-10^6 cm^-3, with isotope/atomic-data nuances.
entries.observational_notes: Usually unresolved at modest resolution and reported as C III] 1908. AGN broad-line density can suppress or alter the doublet.

entries.temperature_regime: photoionized gas around 10000-30000 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Pair with 1907; the ratio approaches atomic low-density and high-density limits and must not be extrapolated beyond them.
entries.observational_notes: Blends with 1907 at common survey resolution; density, C/O, ionization parameter and stellar/AGN continuum are degenerate in equivalent width.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE abundance peaks near 10^5 K; photoionized C IV commonly occurs near 10^4 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Absorption constrains ion column and ionization, not density alone; emission can be resonantly scattered and collisionally excited.
entries.observational_notes: Stronger doublet member. Saturation, unresolved components and partial covering are major column-density systematics; stellar P-Cygni and nebular/AGN emission can blend.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE peak near 10^5 K; also common in cooler photoionized gas
entries.density_sensitivity: No simple critical-density diagnostic in absorption; line ratio tests saturation and radiative transfer.
entries.observational_notes: Weaker member has about half the oscillator strength of 1548. Intrinsic AGN doublet blending depends on line width.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE abundance peaks around 6-8x10^4 K; photoionized gas can be near 10^4 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Primarily column/ionization sensitive; the doublet tests saturation and covering fraction.
entries.observational_notes: Stronger doublet member; stellar-wind contamination and unresolved saturation are common in galaxy spectra.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE peak around 6-8x10^4 K, or cooler photoionized gas
entries.density_sensitivity: Not a direct density probe; doublet ratio and profile constrain opacity and covering.
entries.observational_notes: Weaker member helps reveal saturation; nearby interstellar/stellar features must be modeled in integrated spectra.

entries.temperature_regime: typically cool/warm gas around 10^2-10^4 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Ground-state absorption is column sensitive; excited C II* 1335 lines provide density/cooling constraints when separately measured.
entries.observational_notes: Often saturated even when not black because of unresolved velocity structure or partial covering; emission infill can reduce apparent absorption.

entries.mechanism: permitted resonant transition; recombination/collisional emission and absorption
entries.temperature_regime: neutral/photoionized gas around 10^4 K is common, but absorption spans broad thermal histories
entries.density_sensitivity: Not a direct density line; forest statistics and damping wings constrain density/column after ionization and radiative-transfer modeling.
entries.observational_notes: Resonant scattering, dust and IGM absorption decouple observed flux/profile from intrinsic production. Geocoronal Ly-alpha contaminates low-redshift work.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE abundance peaks near 3x10^5 K; photoionized O VI may occur at much lower density and temperature
entries.density_sensitivity: Absorption gives column rather than density; combine with H I, path length, aligned ions and models. Emission scales strongly with density.
entries.observational_notes: Stronger member. H2 and interstellar blends, saturation, non-equilibrium cooling and multiphase alignment complicate temperature inference.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE peak near 3x10^5 K, with viable photoionized alternatives
entries.density_sensitivity: No direct density measurement; doublet consistency reveals saturation and blends.
entries.observational_notes: Weaker member is frequently blended with C II 1036, C II* and Galactic H2; fit all contaminants jointly.

tracers: hotter ionized gas than O VI
entries.temperature_regime: CIE abundance peaks near 6-7x10^5 K; low-density photoionized solutions require long path lengths
entries.density_sensitivity: Column/ionization diagnostic, not a direct density line; combine with O VI, H I and adjacent ions.
entries.observational_notes: Usually accessible only after redshifting above the Lyman limit/instrument cutoff. Forest blending and continuum placement dominate weak detections.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE peak near 6-7x10^5 K; photoionized alternatives possible
entries.density_sensitivity: Not direct; weaker doublet member constrains saturation and false-positive blends.
entries.observational_notes: Require velocity-coincident detection with the stronger member when possible; the far-UV forest yields a significant interloper rate.

entries.mechanism: He-like resonance absorption/emission, usually collisional or photoionized plasma
entries.temperature_regime: CIE abundance peaks around 2x10^6 K; photoionized O VII can occur at lower kinetic temperature
entries.density_sensitivity: The resonance line alone is not a density meter; the forbidden/intercombination ratio in the full He-like triplet is density and UV-field sensitive.
entries.observational_notes: Weak absorption requires high spectral resolution and careful treatment of instrumental features, Galactic foreground, look-elsewhere effects and wavelength calibration.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE abundance peaks around 3x10^6 K; photoionized gas is also common
entries.density_sensitivity: Primarily temperature/ionization and column sensitive; density requires metastable lines, emission measure or photoionization modeling.
entries.observational_notes: The Ly-alpha doublet is often unresolved. Resonant scattering can suppress central emission in optically thick hot atmospheres.

tracers: resonant scattering/turbulence using Fe XVII ratios
entries.temperature_regime: CIE emissivity is strong around 4-7x10^6 K
entries.density_sensitivity: The 15.01/17.05-17.10 complex is more sensitive to resonant scattering and atomic physics than ordinary low-density plasma density; some Fe XVII ratios gain density sensitivity at high densities.
entries.observational_notes: Resonant scattering lowers the central 15.01-A intensity and can constrain turbulence, but plasma-code and line-blend uncertainties must be propagated.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE abundance/emissivity is strong around 4x10^6 K
entries.density_sensitivity: Use the forbidden/intercombination components of the Ne IX triplet for density/UV-field sensitivity; w alone is not sufficient.
entries.observational_notes: Fe XIX-XXI blends can contaminate the triplet in hot plasmas; use a full plasma model at finite spectral resolution.

entries.mechanism: He-like resonance transition in highly ionized plasma
entries.temperature_regime: CIE line emissivity is strong at several 10^7 K
entries.density_sensitivity: The resolved He-like complex and satellite ratios diagnose temperature, ionization age and at high density density; CCD-blended centroids are model dependent.
entries.observational_notes: Quote whether energy refers to the w line or an unresolved Fe XXV complex. Gain calibration and plasma-code choices set velocity/temperature systematics.

entries.temperature_regime: CIE fraction becomes important around 10^8 K; photoionized Fe XXVI also occurs
entries.density_sensitivity: Primarily ionization/temperature and column sensitive; density comes from broader photoionization or time-dependent modeling.
entries.observational_notes: Often unresolved as a doublet; line identification in fast AGN winds can be degenerate with Fe XXV at a different velocity.

entries.mechanism: K-shell fluorescence following photoionization or energetic-particle impact
tracers: black-hole spin through relativistic broadening with a disk model
entries.temperature_regime: cold or weakly ionized material illuminated by photons above the Fe K edge; not a thermal-excitation temperature line
entries.density_sensitivity: Equivalent width and Compton shoulder constrain column, abundance and geometry rather than local density uniquely.
entries.observational_notes: The common '6.4 keV line' is a K-alpha doublet and shifts with ionization. Broad profiles require continuum, absorption and relativistic-reflection systematics to be modeled jointly.

entries.transition: two-photon annihilation at the electron rest-mass energy
entries.mechanism: direct annihilation and para-positronium two-photon decay
entries.temperature_regime: line width and positronium fraction probe warm neutral/ionized annihilation media; production is not tied to gas temperature
entries.density_sensitivity: No critical density; annihilation timescale and positronium fraction depend on phase, ionization fraction, grains and density.
entries.observational_notes: The centroid is fixed by rest mass, while astrophysical broadening and the positronium continuum constrain thermalization/annihilation conditions. Diffuse-background modeling is central.

entries.mechanism: radioactive beta-plus/electron-capture decay followed by nuclear gamma de-excitation
tracers: recent massive-star activity over Myr timescales
entries.temperature_regime: decay is independent of thermal excitation; emitting isotope is transported through hot superbubbles and ISM phases
entries.density_sensitivity: No critical density; intensity traces isotope mass and decay, while centroid/width trace bulk motion and turbulence.
entries.observational_notes: Laboratory energy is 1808.65 +/- 0.07 keV. Instrumental background, broad response and diffuse-sky modeling dominate; the mean lifetime is about 1.04 Myr.
